<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2015–present)]]
**[[Security Belt]] forces say a missile fired by the [[Houthi]]s hit a [[military parade]] in the [[Southern Movement|southern separatist]]-held town of [[Dhale|al-Dhalea]], killing at least five people and injuring others. There are no claims of responsibility for the attack. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-yemen-security-blast/blast-hits-military-parade-in-yemen-at-least-five-dead-idUSKBN1YX047 (Reuters)]
*[[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|War in Donbass]]
**The [[Ukrainian government]] and [[separatism|separatist]] rebels [[Prisoner exchange|exchange prisoners]] according to the "all identified for all identified" formula agreed upon during peace talks in [[Paris]] earlier this month. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/ukraine-russia-backed-rebels-swap-prisoners-latest-sign-peace-efforts-n1108281 (NBC)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**Local officials say [[Taliban]] have killed 17 local militiamen in an attack on their base in [[Khwaja Baha Wuddin District|Khwaja Bahauddin District]], [[Takhar Province]]. A Taliban spokesman says they killed 21 gunmen. The Taliban propose a 7 to 10-day nationwide [[ceasefire]], after which a peace deal with the [[United States]] would be signed. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/12/taliban-attack-kills-17-local-fighters-northern-afghanistan-191229100215464.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2019 United States bombing of Kata'ib Hizbollah]]
**The [[United States Air Force]] carries out strikes using [[McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle|F-15E Strike Eagle]] jets and [[unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drone]]s in [[Iraq]] and [[Syria]] in retaliation for the death of an [[Americans|American]] civil contractor in a rocket attack on [[K-1 Air Base]] in [[Kirkuk Governorate]]. The strikes were targeted at the [[Iran]]ian-backed [[Kata'ib Hezbollah]] militia group. A spokesman for Kata'ib Hezbollah, says 19 of its fighters were killed and 35 injured in the American strikes, while vowing to respond. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iraq-security-usa/u-s-strikes-in-iraq-syria-target-iranian-backed-shiite-muslim-militia-group-idUSKBN1YX0GR?il=0 (Reuters)] [https://www.france24.com/en/20191229-us-bombs-militant-group-in-iraq-syria-in-retaliation-for-contractor-s-killing (France 24)] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/us-launches-strikes-in-iraq-and-syria-targeting-iran-backed-militia-pentagon-says/2019/12/29/28c12e22-2a64-11ea-be79-83e793dbcaef_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[Prime Minister of Iraq|Iraqi Prime Minister]] [[Adil Abdul-Mahdi]] condemns the unilateral American bombings inside [[Iraq]], saying the U.S. strikes are a "violation of Iraqi sovereignty", and a "dangerous escalation that threatens the security of Iraq and [[Middle East|the region]]." [https://eu.usatoday.com/story/news/world/2019/12/29/us-strikes-iran-backed-militia-behind-attack-killed-american/2770555001/ (''USA Today'')]
**[[Iran]] warns of consequences after the [[Airstrike|airstrikes]]. The Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman [[Abbas Mousavi]] stated it was "illegal" and "the [[United States]] must accept responsibility of the attack." [https://www.cnn.com/2019/12/30/middleeast/iraq-us-airstrikes-reaction-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Terrorism in Russia]]
**Following a tip-off from the [[United States]], Russia arrests two men planning a [[New Year's Eve]] attack in the city of [[Saint Petersburg]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/vladimir-putin-thanks-donald-trump-for-helping-to-prevent-new-year-terror-attacks-in-st-petersburg-11897814 (Sky News)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)]]
**The death toll of [[December 2019 Mogadishu bombing|the attack in Mogadishu the previous day]] rises to 84 with over 25 others remaining missing. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2019-12/30/c_138667291.htm (Xinhua)]
**The [[United States]] target [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] in a series of [[Airstrike|airstrikes]] that killed four. The strikes were in coordination with the [[Federal Government of Somalia|government of Somalia]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/us-targets-al-shabab-militants-after-deadly-mogadishu-bombing/a-51830689 (DW News)]

;Arts and culture
*The world's oldest [[rhinoceros]], Fausta, dies in [[Tanzania]] at the age of 57. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-50937820 (BBC News)]

;Business and economics
*[[Citizenship Amendment Act protests]]
**The [[India]]n [[Tourism in India|tourism industry]] reports that, as a result of protests, December visits to the [[Taj Mahal]] and the state of [[Assam]] declined by 60% and 90% respectively compared to the same period last year. These declines are also occurring in the midst of general [[Economy of India|economic slowdown in the country]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-india-citizenship-protests-tourism/tourists-stay-away-from-taj-mahal-other-indian-attractions-as-protests-flare-idUSKBN1YX03C?il=0 (Reuters)]
*Over 19 flights are cancelled as a three-day strike at [[Lisbon Airport]] comes to an end. The strike was instigated when airport owner [[Vinci SA|Vinci]] refused to unfreeze wages for the employees. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-portugal-airport-strike/airport-strike-prompts-cancellation-of-flights-to-and-from-portugals-capital-idUSKBN1YX0BV?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Ghana]]ian [[President of Ghana|President]] [[Nana Akufo-Addo]] announces his country will adopt the [[Eco (currency)|eco]] as its new currency, but insists to fellow members of the [[currency union]] that it should not be [[Fixed exchange rate system|pegged]] to the [[euro]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-westafrica-economy/ghana-wants-to-join-new-west-african-currency-but-ditch-euro-peg-idUSKBN1YX0EH?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*An official at [[Bangladesh]]'s [[Directorate General of Health Services (Bangladesh)|health directorate]] says at least 50 people have died of cold-related illnesses in December. A [[cold wave]] sweeps through the country, with a [[List of weather records#Asia coldest|lowest]] recorded temperature of {{convert|4.5|°C|°F}}. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/bangladesh-cold-wave-1.5410074 (Thomson Reuters via CBC)]

;Health and environment
*[[2019 Samoa measles outbreak]]
**The [[Samoan government]] lifts its six-week [[state of emergency]] after a mass [[immunization]] campaign against [[measles]] reduced the death and infection rates. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/12/samoa-ends-measles-state-emergency-infection-rate-slows-191229021559134.html (Al Jazeera)]  

;Law and crime
*[[West Freeway Church of Christ shooting]]
**A man kills two people and injures another at a church in [[White Settlement, Texas]], [[United States]] before being killed by a [[security guard]] and a [[civilian]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/injuries-reported-shooting-texas-church/story?id=67969564 (ABC News)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-50942664 (BBC News)]

**Citizens of [[Guinea-Bissau]] head to the polls in the second round of the country's latest [[List of presidents of Guinea-Bissau|presidential]] [[Elections in Guinea-Bissau|election]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bissau-election/guinea-bissau-votes-in-presidential-run-off-between-two-former-premiers-idUSKBN1YX00V (Reuters)]
